newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest grains prices down in one-sided market.
newsitem.headline: Budapest grains prices down in one-sided market.

text.p: Grains prices fell across the board on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) in light trade with one brokerage on the buying side, dealers said on Friday.
"Order (the brokerage) was the only buyer, at limit-down prices," said Robert Monostori of Agrimpex.
He added that only August milling wheat had a significant turnover.
August milling wheat accounted for the lion's share of grains turnover with 642 contracts with its price finishing at 24,600 forints per tonne, down 300.
The other traded milling wheat maturity finished at 25,220 forints, down 400.
Maize saw light trade for May, July and December with less than 100 contracts changing hands, and all 1997 maturities and July 1998 fell, mostly by the limit.
Monostori said the downward trend was justified both by improving weather and easing Chicago prices.
"Chicago is coming down, the weather is good, everybody thinks current prices are good so everybody wants to sell," he said.
Feed wheat and feed barley prices also went down mostly by the limit, only tradeless May sunflower seed finished higher at 37,000 forints.
